consensus_findings.description: Critical: the new composite validators still disagree on the schema-version discriminator. JSON Schema and TypeScript require the numeric integer 1 exactly, but Pydantic's Literal[1] coerces both JSON true and 1.0 to integer 1 even with ConfigDict(strict=True); the reproduced Python ingress probe accepts and normalizes both values. This breaks the promised cross-runtime acceptance boundary at the field that selects the wire contract version.

Nit: TypeScript applies string maxLength with UTF-16 code-unit length while JSON Schema and Python count Unicode code points. A service_name containing 100 astral characters satisfies the declared maxLength 100 and is accepted by Python, but the mandatory TypeScript parser counts 200 and rejects the same envelope.

Nit: audit_log and workflow_terminal_events still accept all-zero trace IDs (and audit request span IDs) even though the canonical W3C contract now rejects zero identifiers and these rows are specified to persist real trace/span IDs. Invalid zero values can therefore enter retained audit/terminal correlation despite being rejected on queue and attempt rows.

Revision 5 correctly documents structural-schema limits, requires composite ingress validation, adds a branded TypeScript parser with semantic checks, closes the SQL JSON-null bypass, and bounds decimal parsing before BigInt conversion.
